summary: Members can move checked roots to a physical group on the same browser board. The dialog retains the requested order, destination and operation ID through conflict review. Under current write access, store::move_selected_items appends the ordered block and commits positions, revisions, field stamps and the replay receipt together.
evidence: Full serial browser_preview suite: 25 passed in owned headless profiles (22 inherited, three new). The final selection-filtered rerun passed all four matching journeys, including all three new ones.

browser_moves_toolbar_selection_in_request_order: choosing the other Work and pressing Escape kept the checks without a POST. Reopening and confirming the first Work sent [67,59,61]. While the board was locked, the old grid, checks and destination remained visible and a second Confirm did nothing. One POST and one grouped refresh produced [73,77,67,59,61]; reload resolved and read at the same history entry without replay. Filling the mixed header and moving into empty Reserve preserved that five-row order. Fresh connections checked grouped and flat reads, all stored rows, boards, groups, revisions, stamps, provenance and receipts.

browser_reviews_conflicting_selection_move: a peer renamed 61 to Indigo/2. The 409 preserved the dialog without a receipt. Review identified a temporarily unavailable original ID and disabled adoption; after restoration, adoption took the reviewed revisions without writing. A deferred receipt failure returned 500 with the entire pre-attempt snapshot intact. Explicit Confirm after fault removal reused the dialog ID, committed one receipt, and left 61 at Indigo/3, the two other selected roots at 2 and board 201 at 2.

browser_demoted_viewer_cannot_move_selection: demotion after choosing the destination produced one POST 403 followed by a grouped GET 200. Checks survived on the read-only board; Move was disabled and Clear worked. The reloaded Viewer could select without writing. Fresh reads confirmed unchanged records, grants and session with no receipt.

All 21 loopback_board_access cases passed. The new access case checked invalid and oversized lists, stale baselines, foreign/hidden roots and groups, revoked session/membership, inaccessible board, Viewer and route isolation. Emptying a source group at the 500-row projection limit returned 413 and rolled back. The replay case checked populated v6 migration twice, old ordering ties and receipts, one winner across competing host connections, byte-identical replay, changed command/actor/kind refusal and a one-root append.

Locked workspace tests passed (36 tests). Cargo used target-browser-packets. Workspace formatting and git diff --check passed. Clippy passed for the affected libraries and tests; the optional all-targets check stopped on the existing unused open_peer method in the foreground example.

The worker shell denied node --test scripts/run.test.mjs before execution; Node runner regressions remain unverified here. Uncertain acknowledgment, failed post-commit refresh and late visit replies were not separately fault-injected in Chromium.
